title: Whether to keep searching after recording a solution
summary: When valid solutions may still exist among a target node's descendants, returning immediately after recording a solution misses deeper solutions; that early return must be removed so the search continues.
context: The task is to find all paths starting at the root, ending at a node with value 7, and containing no node with value 3. The binary tree shown has 8 nodes: root 1 has left and right children 7 and 3; the left (shallower) 7 has left and right children 4 and 5, with a deeper left child 7 beneath 4; and 3 has left and right children 6 and the right 7. Compared with the seven-node input in the earlier example and accompanying Python code, this figure adds the deeper left child 7 beneath 4; on that seven-node tree, removing the return after recording a solution would not add any solutions.

What is compared here is whether to execute return immediately after recording a solution to end the current recursive branch. Pruning that stops descending at node 3 and normal backtracking after visiting a node's children remain unchanged in both approaches; the template code implements that pruning by rejecting choices with value 3.
description: The left and right panels respectively keep and remove the early return after recording a solution. The table below compares which nodes each search visits and resulting paths; in the right branch, both panels stop descending upon reaching the red node 3, skipping 6 and the right 7.

frames.title: Whether to keep searching after recording a solution
frames.explanation: Only by continuing deeper after recording the shallower 7 can the right panel discover the deeper 7 among its descendants; ending the current branch early misses that solution.
